ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the upper emitter of the BJT is connected to the node labeled 3 V; the base is led out from the left side and is grounded through a resistor labeled 60 kΩ; the collector is on the lower right side and is grounded through a resistor labeled 500 Ω. Reasoning: From the figure, the emitter voltage V_E = 3 V, and the given V_EB = V_E - V_B = 0.6 V, so V_B = 3 - 0.6 = 2.4 V. The base is grounded through a 60 kΩ resistor, therefore I_B = 2.4 V / 60 kΩ = 40 μA. Given β = 50, so I_C = β I_B = 50 × 40 μA = 2 mA. The collector current flows through the 500 Ω resistor, making the collector voltage V_C = I_C × 500 Ω = 2 mA × 500 Ω = 1 V. Therefore V_EC = V_E - V_C = 3 - 1 = 2 V.

method.method_draft: Use the active-region equivalent of the BJT: a controlled collector current source of value βI_B feeding the 500 Ω collector load. The image fixes V_E = 3 V and shows the base resistor to ground, so the given V_EB = 0.6 V makes the base node 2.4 V and therefore sets the control current I_B = 2.4/60 kΩ. The controlled source current is then 50 times this value, or 2 mA. Apply the collector load line of the 500 Ω resistor: V_C = 2 mA × 500 Ω = 1 V. Therefore the emitter-to-collector voltage is V_EC = 3 V - 1 V = 2 V.
